about: DRAFT coach wording, NOT APPROVED. Added 23 October 2026 (Stage G of the design of 25 October 2026, section 3) for the goal version of the build-out activity: the words the renderer (back/src/system/rendering/render-concrete-game.ts) may say for an object a game sets out and for a team that scores at an object, keyed by register vocabulary values (the O2.kind of an object, the V1.kind of a scoring event) and never by an activity, a goal or an element, so no scoring kind or sport noun is written in an engine file (the design's no-exception ratchet: 'New wording for a goal comes from data, never from a branch beside ZONE_ENTRY_EVENT'). Every sentence built from these words is DRAFT, awaiting his approval, and is shown to an administrator as draft wording; none is approved-coach-wording.json, which changes only after his approval. The words follow his rulings, each quoted verbatim with the reply it is filed in ('basis'); where a clause states a rule of the game, the game must entail it where it is said (the renderer's gates, named per clause), and fidelity holds every sentence to the game as it holds every other DRAFT sentence. Read through AUDITS_DIR, so the bundled server finds it in dist/knowledge; build.js copies it. Nothing served for real uses it until the goal version is selectable: its two open decisions (goal suitability, the penalty area) are his. AMENDED 24 October 2026 (R1 and R2, the d27 design's stage R1 and R2, its section 2.8), for his reply filed 27 October 2026, items 3 and 4: the words of the one restart after every dead ball (triggers, deadBallRestart, restartLawNouns) are said in the served zone version too, as he directed for both versions ('I want the same restart principle for both the physical-goal and target-zone versions.'); each is DRAFT, awaiting his approval. AMENDED 24 October 2026 (R3, the d27 design's stage R3), for his reply filed 27 October 2026, item 2 ('I approve no offside for this initial realization, with that modification communicated once to the coach.'): the one sentence for a law an activity departs from without replacing it (departedLaws), said once in the served zone version and the goal version (that it covers the zone version is OUR READING, disclosed to him); DRAFT, awaiting his approval. AMENDED 24 October 2026 (stage L, the d27 design's stage L), for his reply filed 26 October 2026, items 7 and 10, and his reply filed 27 October 2026, item 6 ('The goalkeeper should be visually distinguishable from the outfield players.' 'Where normal soccer rules remain relevant during live play, they should continue to apply unless explicitly modified.'): the Set up sentence for a region bound to an object (boundRegions), what a law the game's account records as applying gives the coach (appliedLaws: the handling inside that region, the goalkeeper's colour) and the normal-rules sentence (normalLaws, now said where nothing is owed); none of them is said in the served zone version, which owes the handling law (his reply filed 27 October 2026, item 5). DRAFT, awaiting his approval. AMENDED 24 October 2026 (stage I, the d27 design's stage I(a)), for his reply filed 26 October 2026, items 4 and 11, and his reply filed 27 October 2026, item 6 ('I agree that the coach should identify the available goal type and dimensions, without the engine inventing them.'): the labels of the choices a coach states a session's objects by (objectChoices) - each authorized object of a kind the Sport Profile pairs a region with, named with its document and size, beside a choice by an attribute value, another object of the kind whose width the coach enters, and none - read by the session's own question (the session form, the review page and the live page; back/src/system/rendering/session-object-choices.ts); no activity text says them. DRAFT, awaiting his approval.

entryShape.normalLaws: { words: the one Coach Details sentence the d26 design holds for the sport's normal laws (whole, no slot: the sport's noun is data here), held: why it is held and not said, basis } - added 23 October 2026 (H2, the d26 design's build step 2, section 3.2: 'One DRAFT Coach Details sentence, "Otherwise, normal soccer rules apply", with the sport noun from data.' 'The served zone text is unchanged until he approves.'). HELD: no renderer reads it; the default-laws account in the administrator's review evidence shows it as held. AMENDED 24 October 2026 (R2, the d27 design's section 2.9, V9: 'the normal-rules sentence is refused where anything is owed'): fidelity reads it too, and refuses any sentence saying it where the game's default-laws account owes an adaptation, or where the game has no account; still no renderer says it (the d27 design's stage L). AMENDED 24 October 2026 (stage L, the d27 design's section 2.8: 'It is served only where the default-laws account owes nothing.'): the renderer says it, as the last clause of How it works ('...; otherwise, ...' after a sentence for a law the activity departs from, else as a sentence of its own), citing defaultLaws.owed, wherever the game's account owes nothing; fidelity refuses it said where anything is owed or no account is carried, and its absence where the account owes nothing; its words carry no final full stop
entryShape.triggers: [{ trigger: a member of the register's trigger vocabulary, phrase: the words said for when a restart on that trigger happens, in the restart sentence's list of moments ('The building team's goalkeeper restarts play: ...'), with the slot {carrier} (the kind of the object played with) and no other, basis }] - added 24 October 2026 (R1, the d27 design's stage R1, its section 2.8: 'The trigger phrases come from data. draft-coach-wording.json gains a triggers map'), for his reply filed 27 October 2026, items 3 and 4, so the ball going out and the coach's stoppages, which now restart play the one way his item 4 gives, are said in that sentence; read before the renderer's own table, and two triggers with the same phrase are said once. Only the triggers the common restart needs are listed; the other restart words of his item 4 (the restart said once for every dead ball, which restarts are no longer used) are the d27 design's stage R2. AMENDED 24 October 2026 (R2, the d27 design's stage R2, its section 2.8): these phrases are the moments of the COMMON restart only - read only for a game whose dead-ball restart policy (register row RP1) is the common value, so a game keeping a restart per trigger is said exactly as before R1 (a ball going out over one line is never said as 'goes out of play' for both, the R1 review's should-fix); said in the order listed here; SCORE and COACH_JUDGED_EPISODE_CONCLUSION are listed too, the latter without the renderer's bracketed '(at a stoppage or while play is on)', which the design drops because under the common restart every coach stoppage restarts play the same way
entryShape.deadBallRestart: { <the register's deadBallRestart common value>: { starts: how the restart's taker starts play, with the slot {taker} and no other, restarts: that the taker restarts play whenever the ball is dead, with the slot {carrier} at most, said after ', and ' and before the moments (the triggers above), noOtherRestarts: the Restarts and ball out sentence saying which of the sport's restarts the activity does not use, with the slot {restarts} (the nouns below, listed) and no other, basis } } - added 24 October 2026 (R2, the d27 design's stage R2, its section 2.8: 'draft-coach-wording.json gains a triggers map, a deadBallRestart.COMMON entry and restartLawNouns, each with his words'), for his reply filed 27 October 2026, item 4. Said only for a game whose dead-ball restart policy is that value, where one group of restarts holds every transition the register's block classes as making the ball dead and the start: the How it works sentence 'The building team's goalkeeper starts play, and restarts it whenever the ball is dead: ...' (the design's 'every time' is 'whenever' here: fidelity's obligation lexicon refuses '(every|each) time'), and, after that group's restart sentences, the Restarts and ball out sentence, from the default-laws account of the game (the laws it records as DEPARTED). Its first part cites restartPolicy.deadBall
entryShape.restartLawNouns: [{ law: the id of a law the Sport Profile's defaultLaws block names, marked restart, noun: the coach's plural noun for that restart (no slot), then: optional words said after '; ' where the noun is said (no slot), basis }] - added 24 October 2026 (R2, the d27 design's stage R2, its section 2.8: 'It names only the restart laws the account records as DEPARTED that have a noun in restartLawNouns'). The nouns are said in the order listed, joined '..., ... or ...'; a restart law with no entry here (the kick-off, the dropped ball) has no noun, because the How it works sentence already says the start and every stoppage. Read by the renderer's Restarts and ball out sentence and by fidelity, which refuses a sentence naming a restart whose law the game's account does not record as departed from, one leaving out a departed restart law that has a noun here, and one said where the game's dead-ball restart policy is not the common value
entryShape.departedLaws: [{ law: the id of a law the Sport Profile's defaultLaws block names that is not a restart law (a restart law is named in the Restarts and ball out sentence, by restartLawNouns), words: the one sentence telling the coach the activity departs from it (whole, no slot: the sport's noun is data here), basis }] - added 24 October 2026 (R3, the d27 design's stage R3, its section 2.8: 'Offside, said once, in both versions: "There is no offside."'), for his reply filed 27 October 2026, item 2 ('with that modification communicated once to the coach'). Said once, in How it works, for a game whose default-laws account (the rendering fixture's) records the law as DEPARTED at some place and as nothing but DEPARTED or NOT_APPLICABLE at any other, citing that law's entry in the account (defaultLaws.laws[<law>]); a game with no account, or one recording the law otherwise, has no such sentence. Read by the renderer and by fidelity (V9: a law departed from for communication is cited by exactly one sentence), which refuses the sentence said where the account does not record the law so, said twice or citing anything else, and refuses its absence where it does
entryShape.boundRegions: [{ function: a member of the register's region-function vocabulary (S4.functions, the row the boundRegions block names), objectKind: a member of the register's O2.kind vocabulary, noun: what the coach calls a region of that function bound to an object of that kind (no slot), sentence: the whole Set up sentence, with exactly the slots {object} (the object's kind), {region} (the noun), {width} and {depth} (the cited pairing's figures, in metres) and no final full stop, basis }] - added 24 October 2026 (stage L, the d27 design's stage L(b): 'The Set up sentence for the box, figures read from the cited pairing (DRAFT)'), for his reply filed 26 October 2026, items 7 and 12. Said once in Set up for a region the game binds to an object (register row S7) whose cited pairing (the rendering fixture's boundRegions) gives exactly the region's realized width and depth, centred on the object and set out from the end line it stands on; cites the region's noun, functions, positions and binding, the object's kind, the pairing and, where the markings are set out once, the region's rectangle in the layout. The noun is also the diagram's label for the region (never the target colour). Read by the renderer, the diagram and fidelity
entryShape.appliedLaws: [{ law: the id of a law the Sport Profile's defaultLaws block names that is no restart law, inRegion: { words: what the law gives the coach inside a region its REGION_BOUND_TO_OBJECT precondition names, said after '; ' at the end of that region's Set up sentence, with the slots {performer} (the name of the specialized performer its SPECIALIZED_PERFORMER_PRESENT precondition names) and {carrier} only, basis }, distinguished: { words: what tells that performer apart, said after '; ' at the end of the Players sentence, with exactly the slot {performer}, basis, also: a law of the sport the clause also rests on } }] - added 24 October 2026 (stage L, the d27 design's stage L(b) and (c)), for his reply filed 26 October 2026, items 7 and 10, and his reply filed 27 October 2026, item 6. Each clause is said only where the game's default-laws account records the law as APPLIES at every place it is accounted for, citing defaultLaws.applied[<law>]: so neither is said in the served zone version, which owes that law (his reply filed 27 October 2026, item 5: no handling statement or restriction is added to it). The design's 'may handle' is 'can handle' here: fidelity's hedge lexicon reads 'may' as making a firm sentence optional. That the colour is said where the handling law applies (and not wherever a goalkeeper plays) is OUR READING: the colour shows who may handle (the d27 design's 3.7(e)), and the zone version's handling is his to decide. Read by the renderer and fidelity
entryShape.objectChoices: [{ kind: a kind the register's sessionResources block lists (a session states its availability of it), authorized: { label: the label of each object of this kind a Sport Profile pairing gives a region for, with exactly the slots {kind} (the kind's name), {document} (the pairing's document) and {size} (its width and height in metres, also in feet where both are a whole number of feet at 0.3048 m per foot, the definition of the foot), basis }, attributeValues: [{ attribute: an attribute the register lists for the kind, value: one of its values, label: the label of the choice stating that value (no slot), basis }], other: { label: the label of the choice whose width the coach enters (no slot), basis }, none: { label: the label of the choice stating none of the kind (no slot), basis } }] - added 24 October 2026 (stage I, the d27 design's stage I(a)), for his reply filed 26 October 2026, item 4 ('I agree that the coach should identify the available goal type and dimensions, without the engine inventing them.'). A choice states the values copied from what it names: an authorized object's type and width exactly as its pairing records them (so the exact width match of the bound-region check needs no tolerance), an attribute value, a width the coach enters, or a count of none; the coach says how many. The height is shown in the label and not stated: no rule reads a stated height (the register's sessionResources note: 'The height is not asked: no authorized entry reads it.'). Read by the session's question (back/src/system/rendering/session-object-choices.ts: the session form, the build's question on the review page and the live page) and by the sentence saying which objects a realization is built for where the session's do not suit it
